next_steps: Redwood to share kernel-rollforward checklist and comms draft by 2027-10-14
Aerolith to provide post-peak p99 traces for 2027-10-11-12 window by 2027-10-15
Schedule canary test for egress shaping on 2027-10-18
action_items: Maya: run 10k request burst test with KV cache warmup script and send raw logs (due 2027-10-15)
Elena: confirm firewall rules and return route table snapshot from VPC (due 2027-10-14)

header:
Date: 2027-10-12
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 49 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: available
Attendees: Jesse Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Omar Liu (Redwood CSM); Samir Rao (CTO - Aerolith), Elena Park (NetOps), Liam O'Connor (Security), Priya Menon (SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on stress test results, egress/fallback behavior, and planned kernel rollforward. Team reviewed p95/p99 regressions during synthetic bursts, noted an RTT spike correlated with cross-AZ routing during peak, and agreed on canary timing and data to collect. Action items assigned for benchmark logs, firewall snapshots, and kernel upgrade checklist.
topics: Fallback routing and circuit breaker behavior
Next canary test and rollback criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We'll try to run 49 minutes, lot to cover. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Samir: Samir here, CTO at Aerolith.
[00:15] Elena: Elena, NetOps.
[00:18] Liam: Liam from security.
[00:20] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:22] Maya: Maya, Redwood SE. Omar with me.
[00:25] Jesse: Cool, cool. Quick agenda — review last week's burst test, fallback behavior we saw, kernel roll plan, and next steps.
[00:35] Samir: Sounds good. We had a fairly visible p99 blip on Saturday during the 10k burst, so curious what you found.
[00:42] Maya: Yeah so we dug in — initial read is the p99 latency correlates with a cross-AZ routing flap on your egress path. The app-level latencies are fine when the prefix hits the local path, but if requests route to the other AZ we see KV cache misses, plus longer TCP handshakes.
[01:05] Elena: To be clear, we didn't change the VPC route tables. But the cloud provider did an internal re-home, I think. We saw a short BGP-like re-route.
[01:14] Jesse: Right, and when that happens Redwood's smart routing should prefer same-AZ endpoints but we had a fallback that allowed requests to land on the remote pool. That's expected but should be within SLO — it went beyond.
[01:28] Priya: The p95 held, but p99 spiked from 120ms to 980ms during the peak window.
[01:36] Maya: There's also an effect of cold KV cache after the route switch. Our prefix caching relies on sticky routing for the same host to keep KV warm; when you flip to remote, the model KV cache has to rebuild and that pushes latency.
[01:54] Liam: Question: do we capture enough telemetry for SOC2? We need tamper-proof logs and proof of retention settings.
[02:02] Omar: We have the telemetry stream, and we keep audit logs. We'll share the retention policy doc after the call but quick answer: yes, it's in the compliance pack — we can set retention to whatever you need within limits.
[02:14] Liam: Ok, please send that.
[02:18] Jesse: Back to the burst — Maya, can you summarize the synthetic test we ran and the logs you collected?
[02:24] Maya: Sure. Test was 10k concurrent requests over 2 minutes, with a lead-in warmup of 5 minutes. We instrumented per-token timings and KV cache hit/miss. Observed 7% KV miss rate during the first 30s after route transition; token generation CPU stayed stable but tail latency grew at the 95-99th percentile because of cold KV lookups and increased queueing. We also saw a handful of TLS renegotiations when endpoints changed.
[02:58] Samir: TLS renegotiations — that's concerning. Is that due to connection pool not being sticky?
[03:04] Maya: Partially. Connection affinity breaks during the route change and we spin up fresh TLS sessions to the fallback pool.
[03:12] Elena: Our NAT/gw timeouts are set to 350s, so we shouldn't be dropping established sessions; seems provider did a re-home at the infra layer.
[03:22] Jesse: We should consider two mitigations: one, enforce stricter routing preference on Redwood side for same-AZ for matching client ranges; two, tune egress shaping to gently shed or queue requests during a fallback.
[03:36] Priya: What's the cost/risk of stricter same-AZ sticky routing? Any capacity problems?
[03:40] Maya: It increases hot spot risk on that AZ under heavy load. That's where adaptive circuit-breaker logic helps — we'd shed excess requests to a backup model variant or return a soft-failure until KV warms.
[03:53] Samir: We prefer graceful degradation over outright latency spikes.
[03:56] Jesse: Agreed. So the canary plan is to run a controlled egress shaping during the next test window. We propose 3 phased runs: 50% load, 80% load, full 100% but with circuit breaker thresholds.
[04:12] Elena: When do you want to run that?
[04:14] Jesse: Looking at calendar — propose Monday 2027-10-18 morning.
[04:18] Priya: Morning works. We'll provision monitoring to stick to that window.
[04:22] Maya: We'll run the load generator from Redwood side so we can reproduce routing transitions and capture per-hop traces.
[04:29] Liam: Please include signed timestamps on traces for audit.
[04:32] Omar: Noted.
[04:34] [04:35] — brief cross talk about scheduling
[04:40] Maya: Another item we dug into — memory pressure on the quantized inference lib during bursts. After 30s of sustained high concurrency we saw memory allocator fragmentation causing small pauses; this contributed to latency jitter.
[04:53] Samir: Is that something in the model runtime or system kernel?
[04:57] Maya: It's primarily in the runtime's allocator but interacts with kernel-level reclaim. We have a minor kernel+libquant patch that reduces fragmentation and improves small-allocation latency. It's a non-disruptive update but requires careful canarying.
[05:12] Jesse: We prepared a rollforward checklist: pre-checks, canary subset, rollback steps, and communication stub. We'll send that after the call.
[05:22] Elena: We need to coordinate maintenance windows for the pilot nodes; some of our compliance watchers treat any kernel bump as a maintenance event.
[05:31] Jesse: Understood. The plan is to do the kernel+libquant canary on 10% of nodes in a non-prod subset first. If p95/p99 hold and no telemetry red flags, expand to 50% then to full. Rollback uses image tag revert and a quick cache warmup.
[05:50] Priya: How long is cache warmup expected to take after a revert? We can't have 20-minute degradations.
[05:57] Maya: With our warmup script you can expect normal KV hit rates within 45-90 seconds for typical traffic patterns. For worst-case cold it's a couple minutes.
[06:08] Samir: Acceptable, but add a step to pre-warm on the canary pool before switching production routing.
[06:13] Maya: Agreed, pre-warm will be in checklist.
[06:16] [06:18] — noise, someone muted/unmuted
[06:22] Liam: On telemetry and SOC2, quick note: we cannot persist raw PII-containing prompts beyond 30 days. We need redwood to redact PII at ingest or keep only hashes.
[06:33] Omar: For pilot telemetry we can configure redaction. We'll share the specific telemetry filters — we have a PII redaction pipeline.
[06:41] Liam: Send that to me and legal.
[06:43] Jesse: We'll include the redaction rules in the compliance pack.
[06:47] Maya: Also, on fallback behaviour — we saw an unexpected routing where the fallback pool was at a lower capacity profile; that changed quantization profile and slightly increased cpu per-token. We'll propose ensuring fallback model variants match runtime profile or we auto-scale the fallback pool.
[07:06] Elena: Matching instance types for fallback is our preference. Auto-scaling is ok but can be slower during abrupt flaps.
[07:13] Maya: Right, so config change: add a policy to keep a small hot standby pool with the same instance class, and then auto-scale beyond that if needed. That reduces cold-start effect.
[07:25] Jesse: We'll add that policy to the pilot config and push as a one-line change.
[07:29] Samir: Can you quantify cost delta for a hot standby? We need ballpark numbers.
[07:33] Jesse: Roughly 5-8% additional infra at current pilot sizes; we'll give a more precise projection after you confirm node counts.
[07:41] Priya: Node counts: 12 production pilot nodes across three AZs.
[07:46] Jesse: Ok we'll send delta for 12 nodes.
[07:49] [07:50] — short pause while someone types
[07:55] Maya: Quick note on the TLS renegotiation: we can reduce chest cost by increasing keepalive and using session resumption. But session resumption depends on affinity.
[08:07] Elena: We can relax LB timeouts to keep sessions longer; need to check how that affects our NAT pools.
[08:13] Samir: Also, let's double-check if the provider's re-home events have any RCA publicly; we don't want recurring flaps.
[08:21] Jesse: Good call. We'll add a step for Aerolith to raise support case with the provider and include timestamps from our traces.
[08:29] Maya: Now, regarding the kernel+libquant patch — we have two variants: conservative (smaller wins, fewer changes) and aggressive (bigger perf improvement but slightly higher risk). Conservative gives ~10-15% reduction in small allocation latency, aggressive ~25% but we recommend only in non-critical footprints initially.
[08:52] Priya: Given this is pilot, we prefer conservative first.
[08:55] Samir: Same. No reason to push aggressive yet.
[08:59] Jesse: Conservative it is. We'll prepare the images and the rollforward plan.
[09:03] Maya: We'll also instrument a few additional histograms: per-token alloc latency, TLS session churn, and KV miss waterfall by client subnet.
[09:13] Liam: Please ensure histograms are anonymized and only aggregated — security needs to see patterns not raw prompts.
[09:19] Omar: Will do.
[09:21] [09:23] — small side conversation about log retention policies
[09:29] Elena: One more networking item — MTU mismatch was flagged in last week's packet dump; could contribute to fragmentation during high payload responses.
[09:39] Maya: Yes we saw occasional ICMP fragmentation messages; we'll add an MTU probe in the next test.
[09:44] Priya: Good.
[09:46] Jesse: Ok recapping next steps: Maya to run burst test with warmup and send raw logs by 10/15; Elena to provide route table snapshot and firewall rules by 10/14; Liam to confirm retention and redaction requirements by 10/20; Redwood to share kernel roll checklist and comms by 10/14; schedule canary for 10/18. Agreed?
[10:14] Samir: Agreed.
[10:16] Elena: Agreed.
[10:18] Priya: Agreed.
[10:19] Liam: Agreed.
[10:20] Jesse: Great. Any other blockers?
[10:23] Samir: None from me. Quick ask — can we get an annotated trace example so our infra team can map fields to our toolchain?
[10:31] Maya: We'll send a sample with field docs.
[10:33] Omar: Also sending pricing delta for hot standby for 12 nodes.
[10:37] Jesse: Perfect. We'll follow up with the checklist and the canary run plan. Thanks everyone.
[10:44] Samir: Thanks.
[10:46] Elena: Thanks all.
[10:48] [10:49] — meeting ends

Notes: transcript includes a few mis-hearings and shorthand; speaker labels are approximate, there is occasional cross-talk and filler.
